Add post-weld machining dimensions or a note specifying which features are machined after welding.","recommended_correction":"Add dimensions or a note identifying the features that must be machined to their final sizes after welding is complete."},{"rule_id":"WF-008","evidence":[{"kind":"note","ref":"N1","page":1,"quote":"1) ALL JOINTS TO BE CO2 MIG, FULL WELDED.FILLET SIZE 10 mm."},{"kind":"note","ref":"N3","page":1,"quote":"3) SUITABLE EDGE PREPARATION TO BE DONE."}],"comment":"Note N1 requires full welds but only specifies a fillet size; note N3 defers edge preparation to the shop without giving a bevel angle or root gap. Without defined weld-prep geometry the welder cannot reliably achieve full penetration, risking an incomplete joint. Dimension the bevel angle and root gap for every full-penetration weld, or replace the vague note with specific values.","recommended_correction":"Replace N3 with explicit bevel-angle and root-gap dimensions for each full-penetration weld joint, or add them directly on the views."},{"rule_id":"NM-002","evidence":[{"kind":"note","ref":"N10","page":1,"quote":"10) TO BE TOUGHENED UPTO 28 ~32HRC"},{"kind":"note","ref":"N15","page":1,"quote":"H.T.PROCESS : TOUGHENED HARDNESS & DEPTH : 24 - 32 HRC."}],"comment":"Note N10 limits hardness to 28–32 HRC while note N15 allows 24–32 HRC, so the two notes contradict each other. This leaves inspection without a single acceptance criterion and may cause parts to be accepted or rejected inconsistently.
